from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transformers store facts as coordinates in high-dimensional space.",
            "Imagine a library where similar concepts cluster together.",
            "Vectors represent semantic meaning through spatial proximity."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Vector Embeddings", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 2, 1], y_range=[-1, 2, 1], x_length=4, y_length=4, axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)

        cat_vec = Vector([0.9, 0.1], color="#FF5733")
        dog_vec = Vector([0.1, 0.9], color="#33FF57")
        cat_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(0.9, 0.1), color="#FF5733")
        dog_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(0.1, 0.9), color="#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(Create(axes), GrowArrow(cat_vec.move_to(axes.c2p(0.45, 0.05))), Write(Text("Cat", font_size=20, color="#FF5733").next_to(cat_vec, UP)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(GrowArrow(dog_vec.move_to(axes.c2p(0.05, 0.45))), Write(Text("Dog", font_size=20, color="#33FF57").next_to(dog_vec, UP)))
        self.play(FadeIn(cat_dot), FadeIn(dog_dot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        line = Line(axes.c2p(0.9, 0.1), axes.c2p(0.1, 0.9), color="#3357FF", stroke_width=2)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "MLP layers function as a key-value memory system.",
            "The first layer acts as a pattern matcher.",
            "The second layer projects information to the output space.",
            "Input 'France' activates specific key-value pathways.",
            "Resulting output retrieves the concept 'Paris'."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Anatomy of an MLP: Key-Value Pairs", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # MLP layers function as a key-value memory system.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        rect = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#FF5733")
        label = Text("MLP", font_size=24)
        mlp_block = VGroup(rect, label)
        self.place_at_grid(mlp_block, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(mlp_block))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The first layer acts as a pattern matcher.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        matcher_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.5, color="#33FF57")
        matcher_label = Text("Pattern Matcher", font_size=18)
        matcher = VGroup(matcher_box, matcher_label)
        self.place_at_grid(matcher, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(matcher))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The second layer projects information to the output space.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        projector_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.5, color="#3357FF")
        projector_label = Text("Projector", font_size=18)
        projector = VGroup(projector_box, projector_label)
        self.place_at_grid(projector, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(projector))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Input 'France' activates specific key-value pathways.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF33")
        input_text = Text("France", font_size=24, color="#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(input_text, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        arrow = Arrow(start=input_text.get_right(), end=matcher.get_left(), color="#FFFF33")
        self.play(FadeIn(input_text), GrowArrow(arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Resulting output retrieves the concept 'Paris'.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF33FF")
        output_text = Text("Paris", font_size=24, color="#FF33FF")
        self.place_at_grid(output_text, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=projector.get_right(), end=output_text.get_left(), color="#FF33FF")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Nonlinear Activation as a Switch", [
            "Nonlinear activation functions act as selective switches.",
            "They fire only when input matches specific patterns.",
            "This ensures sparse and modular factual storage."
        ])
        
        # --- Mobjects ---
        # 1. Neuron Gate
        neuron_gate = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.3)
        gate_label = Text("Gate", font_size=24, color="#FF5733")
        neuron_group = VGroup(neuron_gate, gate_label)
        self.place_at_grid(neuron_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)

        # 2. ReLU Function
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-1, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}, x_length=3, y_length=2)
        relu_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: max(0, x), color="#33FF57")
        relu_group = VGroup(axes, relu_curve)
        self.place_at_grid(relu_group, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(FadeIn(neuron_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.play(Create(relu_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        # Flash animation
        self.play(neuron_gate.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.8).set_color("#3357FF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(neuron_gate.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.3).set_color("#FF5733"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers
outline.target_audience: University students with a foundational understanding of machine learning and neural networks.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Vector Embeddings
sections.content: Briefly explain that MLPs don't store text like a database; they store 'concepts' as coordinates in high-dimensional space. Visualize this as a library where similar facts are clustered together.
sections.example: Represent 'Cat' as a point [0.9, 0.1] and 'Dog' as [0.1, 0.9] on a 2D coordinate plane.

sections.title: The Anatomy of an MLP: Key-Value Pairs
sections.content: Explain that an MLP block in a Transformer acts as a 'key-value memory.' The first linear layer acts as a 'pattern matcher' (Key), and the second layer projects the result back to the vocabulary space (Value).
sections.example: Input: 'The capital of France is...' -> Pattern Matcher activates the 'France' neuron -> Value projector outputs 'Paris'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Nonlinear Activation as a Switch
sections.content: Introduce the ReLU or GeLU activation function. Explain it as a gate that only fires if the input matches a specific stored pattern, ensuring that factual storage is sparse and modular.
sections.example: Visual animation: A 'neuron' gate remains closed (0) until the input vector crosses a specific threshold, then snaps open to inject the factual information 'Paris'.

sections.title: Dynamic Synthesis: From Weights to Facts
sections.content: Explain that a single fact is not stored in one neuron, but distributed across the weights of the entire MLP layer, acting like a holographic image.
sections.example: If the model learns 'The sky is blue,' it modifies weights across multiple layers. If you 'mute' one neuron, the fact remains; mute the whole layer, and the fact disappears.

sections.title: Application: Editing the Model’s Knowledge
sections.content: Summarize how researchers can perform 'Model Editing' by surgically altering the specific weights in an MLP layer to update an outdated fact without retraining the whole network.
sections.example: Updating a model that thinks 'The President of the USA is X' by mathematically shifting the weights associated with that specific MLP layer to point to 'Y' instead.
